title: Boudhanath Stupa
summary: Boudhanath is the largest stupa in Nepal, on the plain about 8 km from Kathmandu, topped by a square tower painted with the eyes of the Buddha. Its origins are dated to the 5th century, with chronicles naming Licchavi kings, and it has been renovated many times. It is part of the Kathmandu Valley World Heritage property.

uncertainty.note: ICOMOS says the origins date to the 5th century; chronicles cited by a travel page name kings from about AD 400 to 505, and other traditions on the same page give later dates up to AD 604. The origin date is not securely established.

as_recorded.value: The origins of the stupa date to the 5th century.

when.display: Origins in the 5th century (tradition); renovated many times

importance.justification: The largest stupa in Nepal and one of the seven ensembles of the Kathmandu Valley World Heritage property.

sources.title: Kathmandu Valley (Nepal) No 121 rev: ICOMOS evaluation

reviewer_note: Origin date rests on chronicles; the travel page itself says sources disagree (founders from c. AD 400 to 604). No institutional height was found, so no model.
